title.zh: 鞠躬的人与脱帽的人：1783年的一次权力交还
title.en: The Man Who Bowed and the Men Who Kept Their Hats On: Handing Back Power, 1783

dek.zh: 总司令到国会交还委任状。国会在前一天把谁坐着、谁鞠躬、谁脱帽逐条写进日志——交接的形式本身，就是交接内容的一部分。
dek.en: The commander in chief came before Congress to hand back his commission. The day before, Congress wrote into its journal exactly who would sit, who would bow, and who would lift a hat. The form of the handover was part of what was being handed over.

heading.zh: 一、收场比开战更需要规矩
heading.en: I. Wrapping Up Takes More Rules Than Waging War

paras.zh: 1783年12月22日，星期一，大陆会议议定了第二天公开接见总司令乔治·华盛顿的次序。难处不在打仗，而在收场：一个统帅军队的人要当众把受托的权力交回一个坐着开会的机构，这个场面里谁坐着、谁站着、谁鞠躬、谁脱帽，本身就在说话。国会为此把接见的动作逐条写定。
paras.en: On Monday, 22 December 1783, the Continental Congress settled the order of the next day's public audience with its commander-in-chief, George Washington. The hard part was not the fighting but the ending. A man who had commanded armies was about to hand delegated power back in public, to a body that did its business sitting down, and in a scene like that, who sits, who stands, who bows and who lifts a hat all speak for themselves. So Congress wrote the movements of the audience down, item by item.

heading.zh: 二、先写好动作，再等将军上门
heading.en: II. Write the Moves First, Then Wait for the General

paras.zh: 议定的接见次序一共三条。第一条：议长与议员就座，并且戴着帽子，秘书立于议长身旁。第二条：将军到达时，由传信人通报秘书，秘书随即引入将军及其随行副官进入会议厅。第三条：将军由秘书引导至座位，落座，两侧各立一名副官，秘书回到自己的位置。坐着的、戴帽的、站着的、入场的，各有各的位置。
paras.en: The agreed order of the audience ran to three clauses. First, the President and the members were to sit, covered — that is, wearing their hats — with the secretary standing at the President's side. Second, the General's arrival was to be announced to the secretary by a messenger, who would then introduce the General, attended by his aides, into the Hall of Congress. Third, the secretary would conduct the General to a chair and he would be seated, an aide standing on either side of him, while the secretary resumed his own place. Sitters, hat-wearers, standers, entrants: everyone had an assigned position.

paras.zh: 另一条规矩专门管身体动作：「When the General rises to make his address, and also when he retires, he is to bow to Congress, which they are to return by uncovering without bowing.」——将军起身致辞时、退场时，都要向国会鞠躬；国会以脱帽回礼，不鞠躬。按这条规矩，鞠躬的只有将军一人，国会以脱帽回礼。
paras.en: One further rule governed bodily gesture alone: "When the General rises to make his address, and also when he retires, he is to bow to Congress, which they are to return by uncovering without bowing." He would bow when he rose to speak and again when he withdrew, and Congress would answer by removing their hats, without bowing back. Under this rule only the General bowed; Congress answered by raising their hats.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，国会把这场交接的性质先写进了姿态里：讲话的人起身、鞠躬、陈述、退出，听取的人自始至终坐着，只把帽子摘一下。权力不是在讲话文本里才交还的，在鞠躬与脱帽的不对称里已经交还了一半。这是作者的解释；日志只记规则，不写理由。
paras.en: One reading of this is that Congress wrote the nature of the transaction into posture before a word was spoken. The speaker rises, bows, gives his account, and withdraws; the listeners remain seated throughout and do no more than lift a hat. Power is not returned only in the text of a speech; half of it is already returned in the asymmetry between the bow and the uncovered head. That is the author's reading. The journal records the rules and gives no reasons.

heading.zh: 三、十二月二十三日：停顿、致辞、交出委任状
heading.en: III. December 23: The Pause, the Address, the Commission

paras.zh: 第二天，12月23日，星期二，接见按议定次序进行。日志的写法很省：按既定次序，总司令获准入内，举行公开接见。
paras.en: The next day, Tuesday, December 23, the audience proceeded in the agreed order. The journal is spare about it: according to order, the Commander in Chief was admitted to a public audience.

paras.zh: 他落座之后，会场宣布肃静。议长停顿片刻，然后告知他，合众国代表组成的国会已准备好听取他的陈述——「the President, after a pause, informed him, that the United States in Congress assembled, were prepared to receive his communications」。话音落下，他起身发言。那片刻停顿是被记下来的：议长没有立刻接话，沉默本身被写进了官方记录。
paras.en: Once he was seated, silence was ordered, and the President let a pause go by before telling him that the United States in Congress assembled were prepared to receive his communications. The journal puts it this way: "the President, after a pause, informed him, that the United States in Congress assembled, were prepared to receive his communications". The pause made it into the record. The President did not rush to fill the silence; the silence itself was entered into the official account alongside the words. Then the General rose and spoke.

paras.zh: 讲话开宗明义交代来意：「The great events on which my resignation depended, having at length taken place」——他辞职所等待的大事终于发生，他向国会致贺，并把自己带到国会面前，「to surrender into their hands the trust committed to me」，把所受的托付交还国会手中，同时「to claim the indulgence of retiring from the service of my country」，请求允准他退出国家的服务。请辞用的是请求允准的说法，而非通知生效。
paras.en: The address declared its business in the first line: "The great events on which my resignation depended, having at length taken place" — the events his resignation had been waiting on had finally occurred. He offered Congress his sincere congratulations and presented himself before them "to surrender into their hands the trust committed to me", returning the trust placed in him to their hands, and at the same time "to claim the indulgence of retiring from the service of my country", asking their indulgence to withdraw from the service of his country. Note the register of the request: he asks leave to retire rather than announcing that he has.

paras.zh: 接着他说，在独立与主权得到确认之际，他欣然辞去当初怀着疑虑接受的任命：「I resign with satisfaction the appointment I accepted with diffidence」。接受时怀着疑虑，交还时感到满意，这是他自己的说法。至于说这话时是什么语气，日志无从体现，本篇也不猜。
paras.en: He went on: happy in the confirmation of independence and sovereignty, he resigned with satisfaction the appointment he had accepted with diffidence — "I resign with satisfaction the appointment I accepted with diffidence". Diffidence at the start, satisfaction at the end: those are his own words. What tone his voice carried is beyond the reach of the journal, and this piece will not guess.

paras.zh: 结尾把话说完：「Having now finished the work assigned me, I retire from the great theatre of action」——如今已办完交给他的工作，退出伟大的行动舞台；向这个他长期奉命行事的庄严机构道别，「I here offer my commission」，在此交出委任状，并辞去公职生涯的一切职务。
paras.en: The close said the rest: "Having now finished the work assigned me, I retire from the great theatre of action" — the work assigned to him was finished, and he was withdrawing from the great theatre of action. He bid an affectionate farewell to the august body whose orders he had so long followed, "I here offer my commission", and took his leave of every employment of public life.

paras.zh: 说完，他走上前，把委任状和讲稿副本一并交给议长。日志以一句话收尾：「He then advanced and delivered to the President his commission, with a copy of his address」。委任状是权力的凭证，副本是说法的留档，两件东西一次交清。至此，仪式有了实物的落点。
paras.en: With that, he stepped forward and placed his commission, together with a copy of his address, in the President's hands. The journal closes the entry in one line: "He then advanced and delivered to the President his commission, with a copy of his address". The commission was the token of authority; the copy was the account of it, kept on file. Two objects, delivered at once. The ceremony now had something physical to land on.

paras.zh: 作者推断，这套流程的要害在于它不依赖任何人相信谁的品格：仪式前一日成文，次日照章执行，凭证当场易手，文字随凭证入档。一个人是否忠诚，十分钟的场面无法证明；但权力是否已归位，可以在这一天被记成白纸黑字。这是作者对记录方式的解释，日志本身并未陈述其用意。
paras.en: The author's inference is that the point of the procedure was that it depended on nobody's character. The order was written the day before, executed to the letter the next day, the token changed hands on the spot, and the words went into the archive along with it. A man's loyalty cannot be proven by ten minutes of ceremony. Whether power has been put back where it belongs, however, can be entered in black and white on a particular day. That is an interpretation of how the record was made; the journal itself states no such intention.

heading.en: IV. What the Form Is Arguing

paras.zh: 把这次交还和一般的口头表态分开看，可以看出三件事同时在进行。其一，次序是事先写定的：22日议定，23日执行，现场没有临时调整的记录。其二，礼节是不对称的：将军起身致辞和退场时鞠躬，国会以脱帽回礼，站着的鞠躬、坐着的回礼，高低位差被明确保留。其三，交出的是实物——委任状，外加讲稿副本。仪式、姿态、凭证三者叠加，才构成这一次有记录的权力交还。
paras.en: Set this handover beside an ordinary spoken one and three things are happening at once. First, the sequence was fixed in advance: agreed on the twenty-second, carried out on the twenty-third, with no record of last-minute adjustment. Second, the etiquette was asymmetric: the General was to bow when he rose to speak and when he withdrew, and Congress to answer by uncovering: the standing man bowed, the seated body answered. The vertical distance between them was kept deliberately visible. Third, what changed hands was physical: the commission, plus a copy of the address. Ceremony, posture, and token together make up this documented transfer of power.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，鞠躬与脱帽之间的差额不是羞辱，而是定位：国会要让在场者看见，军队的统帅向这个机构低头，而这个机构不必向统帅低头。议员们戴着帽子坐着这一点尤其醒目——作者的理解是：戴帽落座、让对方站着讲话，像是在现场画出“我们是听取汇报的一方”。这条解释是作者提出的；日志只写了戴帽与就座，没写为什么。
paras.en: On one reading, the gap between bowing and uncovering is not an insult but a placement. Congress wanted those present to see the commander of the army incline himself to this institution, while the institution owed him no inclination in return. The covered, seated members are the striking detail. As the author reads it, men sitting with their hats on while another stands to address them draw a line in the room: we are the ones receiving the report. That explanation is the author's. The journal notes covering and seating, and no more.

paras.zh: 作者提出的替代设想（非史实）：这场交接完全可以设计成别的样子。比如将军与议长相向而立、各自致辞；或者由秘书代读交还文书，将军本人不必到场；再或者只收下委任状，不设讲话环节。这些做法同样能完成权力归位，甚至更快，但都会少掉一个可见的高低位差和一段被完整记录的自述。作者列在这里，是为了说明形式并非只有一种解；实际采用的是这一种。
paras.en: An alternative design the author offers (not history): this handover could have been arranged quite differently. The General and the President might have faced each other and spoken in turn; the secretary might have read the surrender of the commission aloud with the General absent; or Congress might simply have taken the commission, with no speech at all. Each version would have restored the authority, perhaps faster, and each would have cost a visible ranking and a complete first-person account. The list is here to show that the form was not the only possible one; the one that happened is the one Congress adopted.

paras.zh: 现代场景一：一个开源项目的首席维护者决定退居幕后，把仓库的管理权限交回社区委员会。交接排在一次视频会议里，马上冒出一串问题：谁主持、谁先说话、屏幕共享显示哪一块、权限是当场点“移交”还是散会后各自操作。把这些提前写进议程，交接就不靠任何人的风度；不写，交接就变成谁嗓门大、谁在线谁说了算。
paras.en: A modern scene, first. The lead maintainer of an open-source project decides to step back and hand the repository's administrative rights back to the community council. The handover is scheduled for a video call, and a queue of questions appears at once: who chairs, who speaks first, which window gets shared, and whether the rights are transferred by clicking "transfer" live on the call or by each side poking at settings afterwards. Put those answers into the agenda in advance and the handover depends on nobody's good manners. Leave them out and it becomes a contest of volume and availability.

paras.zh: 现代场景二：咨询项目结项，顾问把客户在项目期间给过的账号、文档、门禁卡逐项交还。行政人员在签收单上一条条打钩，每件写清名称和日期。这张单子平时没人看，但两年后若要回答“那批权限当时到底收回没有”，能拿出来的东西只有它。凭证加清单，比一场气氛融洽的道别更耐用。
paras.en: A modern scene, second. A consulting engagement closes, and the consultant returns, item by item, the accounts, documents, and building passes the client issued over the life of the project. An administrator ticks them off a receipt sheet, each line naming the item and its date. Nobody looks at that sheet on an ordinary day. Two years on, if someone has to answer the question of whether those access rights were in fact recovered, the sheet is the only thing that can be produced. A token plus a list outlasts a warm and cordial goodbye.

heading.zh: 六、这份记录没有告诉我们的
heading.en: VI. What This Record Does Not Tell Us

paras.zh: 本篇所据只有《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录：12月22日议定的接见次序、23日的接见经过与讲话文本。没有取得任何在场者的私人记述，因此讲话者的神情与语气、在场者的反应，一律付之阙如。日志记动作、记次序、记讲话，不记心情；本篇也不涉及他此后的事。凡是原文没写的动机、念头和“他考虑过的选项”，本篇都不替他补。
paras.en: Everything in this piece rests on one source: the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 — the order of audience agreed on December 22, the audience of the twenty-third, and the text of the address. No private account by anyone present was consulted, and so the speaker's face and tone, and the reactions in the room, are simply absent. The journal records gestures, sequence, and speech; it does not record feeling. Nor does this piece follow the man beyond that day. Motives, private thoughts, and options he may have considered are never supplied by this writer where the source is silent.

paras.zh: 另有两处技术性保留。第一，议长的答词没有收进本篇证据包，本篇不予引用。第二，这份材料取自影印本的OCR识别，存在讹字，本篇英文引文只取清晰片段，可疑拼写一律留在引号之外。引用越短，越要干净。
paras.en: Two technical reservations follow. First, the President's reply is not in this article's evidence pack and is not quoted. Second, the material comes from OCR of a facsimile and contains misreadings, so the English quotations here take only clean stretches, with doubtful spellings left outside the quotation marks. The shorter the quotation, the cleaner it must be.

scenario.zh: 公司里一个临时项目组解散，组长要把项目期间被授予的审批权和对外签字权交回原部门。交接要在一次二十分钟的会上完成，双方之后仍要共事。
scenario.en: A company dissolves a temporary project team, and the team lead must hand back the approval authority and external signing power granted during the project to the departments that lent it. The handover has to be completed in one twenty-minute meeting, and both sides will keep working together afterwards.

question.zh: 交接会上，是让交权的人站起来逐项说明、坐着的人确认接收，还是大家围坐闲聊两句、散会后补一封邮件？如果两种都能把事办完，你会选哪一种来留下记录——你希望日后被追问“权限到底收回来没有”时，手里握着的是一张签收单，还是一段谁也说不清的记忆？
question.en: At the handover meeting, do you have the person giving up authority stand and walk through each item while the receiving side sits and confirms, or does everyone chat around the table for two minutes and send a follow-up email afterwards? If both get the job done, which one do you choose for the record it leaves — when someone someday asks whether those permissions were actually recovered, do you want to be holding a signed receipt sheet, or a memory no one can reconstruct?

assumptions.zh:
交接双方都要在场，且此后仍需合作
权限收回必须留下可核查的记录
会议只有二十分钟，做不成大仪式
assumptions.en:
Both sides will be present and must continue cooperating afterwards
The return of the permissions must leave a checkable record
The meeting lasts twenty minutes; there is no room for a grand ceremony

steps.zh:
会前一天把交接次序写成几条发给双方：谁主持、谁先说、交出哪几项
会上由接收方坐着听取说明，交出方逐项宣读要交回的权限与物品
当场在权限清单上签字，副本同时归档，散会后不再以口头方式补充
steps.en:
The day before, write the order of the handover in a few lines and send it to both sides: who chairs, who speaks first, and which items are being surrendered
At the meeting, the receiving side sits and listens to the account while the departing side reads out each permission and item being returned
Both sides sign the permissions list on the spot, a copy is filed immediately, and nothing is added by word of mouth afterwards

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：不开专门会议，只发一封附清单的交接邮件，双方各自点确认。更快、更不显眼，但可核查的只剩那封邮件，没有一个双方共同在场的确认时刻。
alternative.en: Another approach the author would suggest: hold no dedicated meeting at all, just send a handover email with the list attached and have each side click confirm. Faster and less conspicuous, but the only checkable artifact is that one email, with no moment of joint confirmation in the same room.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部事实来自《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录（1783年12月22日议定的接见次序、12月23日的接见与华盛顿讲话文本）。没有在场者私人记述可对照，人物心情与现场反应不可知；议长答词在该卷中以带删改痕迹的草稿形式印出，本篇未引用；材料经OCR识别，存在讹字，引文只取清晰片段。
uncertainty_note.en: All facts come from the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 (the order of audience agreed on December 22, 1783; the audience and Washington's address of December 23). No private account by anyone present was available for comparison, so mood and reaction in the room are unknowable; the President's reply is printed in that volume as a draft bearing signs of revision and is not quoted here; the material was captured by OCR from a facsimile and contains misreadings, so quotations take only clean stretches.
